transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call - we got Marco from SE, Jenna on CSM side. Mark, Priya, Liam from AstraHealth?
[00:10] Mark (AstraHealth): Yep hi all, thanks.
[00:12] Priya: morning - afternoon for some of us, hi.
[00:15] Sofia: Cool. Agenda — quick run through this week's benchmark numbers vs your baseline provider, dig into a couple of outliers, then action items. Marco will run through the data.
[00:22] Marco (SE): Alright jumping in — I shared the spreadsheet earlier (link in chat: https://redwood.internal/bench/astra-2026). Quick takeaways first: overall throughput (tokens/sec) is up ~20% on average across the inference mix when using our batching + prefix cache vs the baseline; 95th percentile latency for the Llama-variant tests is ~180ms on Redwood vs ~320ms on their provider for the same payload and concurrency. Those numbers are warm-cache — cold starts do increase, we captured that too.
[00:45] Mark: ok those warm numbers look promising. Can you walk me through the test shape? like payload sizes and qps?
[00:52] Marco: Sure — we ran three workloads: short prompts (~50 tokens), medium (~200), long (~800). Concurrency sweep from 1 to 50 concurrent connections. Request payloads included metadata & embeddings in some cases to mimic your traffic. Baseline provider numbers are the same workload run on their mpt-optimized cluster (their config we were given).
[01:15] Priya: one thing we care about is tail latency at the 95/99 for the medium prompts; our users notice spikes.
[01:22] Marco: Right — 95th is where we shine vs baseline; 99th gets closer, about 420ms on Redwood vs 560ms baseline for medium prompts. The gap shrinks for long prompts because effective tokens/sec is dominated by decoding time.
[01:40] Mark: How much of this is quantization? I know you tested int8/int4?
[01:44] Marco: We tested FP16 baseline, int8 and int4 quantized variants. int8 gave ~10-15% throughput boost with negligible quality delta on your eval sets; int4 shows bigger perf but we saw minor quality regression on a subset of prompts — we logged the failure cases.
[02:05] Mark: So if we can't accept any quality regressions, maybe int8 or FP16 for now.
[02:09] Marco: Agreed. Also our KV cache reduced repeated prefix cost by ~35% on medium prompts — that helped tail latency when requests share prefixes.
[02:22] Priya: Are those caching numbers realistic for our traffic? we have lots of short, similar queries hitting the same model.
[02:27] Marco: We used a synthetic workload sampled from the traces you shared last week; caching effectiveness will depend on real overlap, but the sample suggests 30-40% reuse which maps to the 35% number.
[02:40] Jenna (CSM): Quick security question from Liam's earlier note — can you confirm audit logs and KMS integration for the private deployment?
[02:48] Sofia: Yes — we'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts and example audit log formats; we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and dedicated. Jenna will send links after the call.
[03:00] Liam (CTO): For on-prem, we need to run the on-site benchmark with our rack — curious about noise from multi-tenant hardware, how do you account for that?
[03:10] Marco: For on-prem we recommend isolated hosts for the run, or run a controlled low-noise window. Kernel-level profiling and pinned CPU/GPU settings were used in our measurements; we'll share the profiling logs.
[03:27] Mark: The baseline provider had a weird spike in the long prompt throughput at 30 conc — any idea why?
[03:33] Marco: Looks like their autoscaler kicks at that point and you see cold container starts; Redwood's routing kept requests on-warm longer due to longer-lived workers and warm-pooling in dedicated mode; but that is a config that can be tuned either way.
[03:50] Priya: Can we see the distribution of worker lifetimes?
[03:54] Marco: included in the spreadsheet — worker lifetime histogram and cold-start count per run.
[04:02] Mark: What about cost delta? If performance is better but cost is much higher, that's a problem for us.
[04:08] Sofia: Good call — we computed per-token unit cost normalized to throughput; for the warm workloads Redwood is roughly 12% lower cost per useful token vs baseline when using int8 profiles + caching. For FP16 warm run it's closer to parity. We'll include a clearer cost table in the pricing doc we send.
[04:28] Priya: Do you have numbers for 95th latency at 50 concurrent? that's our target scenario.
[04:33] Marco: For medium prompts at 50 conc: Redwood 95th ~240ms (warm), baseline ~420ms. For cold-starts it's 680ms vs 920ms respectively. We'll rerun with stricter concurrency to validate — that's an action item.
[04:52] Mark: Any concerns on model compatibility — we use a few custom fine-tuned checkpoints.
[04:58] Marco: Fine-tunes behaved similarly in our tests; the main caveat is some kernel paths for custom ops might not be as optimized — we flagged one small op in your fine-tune that falls back to slower kernel. We'll propose a fix/optimization and estimate time.
[05:15] Priya: On security: how long do you keep audit logs in Dedicated vs Private? Our compliance needs 1 year retention for certain events.
[05:23] Jenna: Dedicated can retain logs per agreement, and Private you control retention in your storage. We'll include retention options in the security pack.
[05:31] Liam: If we move to Dedicated rather than hosted, does it change the latency profile?
[05:35] Marco: Dedicated typically reduces noise and gives more consistent 95/99 tails because of reduced multi-tenant variance; plus you can reserve warm workers and configure burst pools. We saw better stability in Dedicated runs.
[05:47] Mark: Any blockers on our side for next steps?
[05:50] Priya: We need the exact test harness and ports for the on-site runs, plus confirmation on dataset privacy for the traces we'll share.
[05:58] Sofia: We'll send the harness and a small NDA addendum if needed.
[06:02] Marco: One more note — we observed a weird outlier in the medium prompt run at bs=8: one node had degraded FP16 perf, looks like driver mismatch. We'll rerun that node and exclude anomalies.
[06:16] Mark: ok please do.
[06:18] Sofia: Great — quick recap and next steps: Marco reruns the 50-concurrency 95th test and batch sweep; Jenna will send security docs; Sofia will send pricing and profiling logs. We'll tentatively schedule the on-site run week of Nov 15. Anything else?
[06:34] Liam: No, that covers it. Thanks everyone.
[06:36] Priya: Thanks.
[06:37] Sofia: Thanks all, bye.
